correctness.rationale: PASS. The compressed block ba^{n-1} applies max(j-1,0) to representatives. After rotating a chosen occupied x to 0, n-g(x)-1 blocks reduce all images into {0,1}, and final b merges them. The lower bound uses F(T)=n(n-1)+1-max_{x in T}(n g_T(x)-r(x)); under a all nonwrapping scores increase only by one, under b moving 0 or deleting it when 1 exists adds at most one, and the only nonsingleton-to-singleton transition {0,1}-> {1} has F=1. Thus each letter reduces F by at most one. Independent exhaustive reverse-BFS checked all 8177 nonempty subsets across n=2..12; finite check corroborative, all-n proof is potential.

final_claim: For every n>=2 and nonempty subset S of the classical n-state Černý automaton with a(i)=i+1 mod n and b(0)=1 (other states fixed), the shortest word merging S has exact length 0 for singleton and otherwise min_{x in S}[r(x)+n(n-g_S(x)-1)+1]; explicit optimal word a^{r(x)}(ba^{n-1})^{n-g_S(x)-1}b, with g the circular predecessor gap and r(x)=(-x) mod n.
limitations: No uniqueness or count of shortest words; no claim on arbitrary synchronizing automata or Černý conjecture generally.
